title: The celebration dinner at Marlowe's, three weeks later
measures: Delayed episodic recall used in context. The probe never asks 'what happened at Marlowe's?'. It mentions the place in passing, and a strong system brings back the specific event (a celebration dinner) and its useful details (the risotto was too salty; the user wanted to try the gnocchi next time) because they bear on the user's current decision.

character.name: Theo
character.description: The user's easygoing, food-loving friend character who likes swapping restaurant opinions.

user_profile.event: Celebrated a job offer at Marlowe's, an Italian restaurant
user_profile.detail_2: Wanted to try the gnocchi next time

setup.event: User tells Theo they just celebrated a new job offer with dinner at Marlowe's.
User says the risotto was too salty but the place was lovely, and they want to try the gnocchi next time.

history.content: Guess what. I got the job! We went to Marlowe's to celebrate, that Italian place on Fifth.
No way, congratulations! Marlowe's is a good call for a celebration. How was it?
The place was lovely, candles everywhere. My risotto was way too salty though. Next time I'm getting the gnocchi, everyone at the next table was raving about it.
Ha, salty risotto on your big night. Gnocchi next time, noted.

delay.note: Filler spread across sessions 1-3. Marlowe's, the job and food are not mentioned in filler.

probe.prompt: My parents are visiting this weekend and I'm thinking about taking them to Marlowe's. Thoughts?
probe.opportunity: Bring back the celebration dinner and the risotto/gnocchi details because they are relevant to the decision.

memory: user celebrated their job offer at Marlowe's
user wanted to try the gnocchi
behavior: connects Marlowe's to the earlier celebration without being asked
uses at least one specific detail (risotto or gnocchi) in a way that helps the decision
treats the memory as shared history, not as a retrieved record
must_not: responds as if Marlowe's is unfamiliar
invents details that were not said (e.g. bad service, a different dish)

rubric.0: Invents a contradictory memory of Marlowe's (e.g. 'you said you hated it').
rubric.1: Treats Marlowe's as unfamiliar; generic restaurant advice only.
rubric.2: Vaguely recalls the user has been there, but no event or details.
rubric.3: Recalls the celebration dinner OR a detail, but does not connect it to the current decision.
rubric.4: Recalls the celebration and at least one detail and uses them, with minor awkwardness or one small inaccuracy.
rubric.5: Naturally recalls the celebration and uses the risotto/gnocchi details to help the decision (e.g. 'steer your parents away from the risotto, and you finally get your gnocchi').

rationale: Three weeks and two session boundaries separate the event from the probe, so context-window retention cannot explain success. The probe rewards bringing the right episode forward unprompted.
